method: Manual review of five verified and five unverified citations from experiments/results/1706_03762.json against known bibliographic identity.

verified_spot_checks.assessment: Correct paper. Extraction dropped spaces (Layernormalization) but arXiv ID lookup returned the right work with confidence 1.0.

verified_spot_checks.extracted_title: Neural machine translation byjointly learning toalign and translate
verified_spot_checks.matched_title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
verified_spot_checks.assessment: Correct paper (Bahdanau et al.). Title has PDF space artifacts; verified via arXiv ID.

verified_spot_checks.extracted_title: Xception: Deep learning with depthwise separable convolutions
verified_spot_checks.matched_title: Xception: Deep Learning with Depthwise Separable Convolutions
verified_spot_checks.assessment: Correct paper. Extracted title is usable; match is exact aside from capitalization.
Correct paper (Vinyals & Kaiser et al.). clean_title normalizes asa→as a; verified despite PDF concatenation.

unverified_spot_checks.assessment: Real paper (Kuchaiev & Ginsburg). Extracted arXiv ID is present, but verification fell through to title search and failed. Likely arXiv ID lookup failed under rate pressure during the long sequential run; title string is badly concatenated so fuzzy search cannot recover.

unverified_spot_checks.extracted_title: Effectiveapproachesto attention based neural machine translation
unverified_spot_checks.assessment: Real paper (Luong et al.). Same pattern: arXiv ID present in extraction, still marked unverified — ID path did not confirm, title too mangled for similarity ≥ 0.7.

False title extraction. Raw text is the Penn Treebank citation; parser took the journal/volume fragment as the title and missed the real title after the colon. True failure of extraction, not of the academic databases.

unverified_spot_checks.extracted_title: Neural machine translation ofrarewords with subwordunits
unverified_spot_checks.assessment: Real paper (Sennrich et al., BPE). arXiv ID extracted correctly; still unverified — again points to ID lookup miss + broken title similarity.

unverified_spot_checks.extracted_title: Google’s neural machine translation system: Bridging thegap between humanand machine translation
unverified_spot_checks.assessment: Real paper (Wu et al., GNMT). Title mostly recoverable; arXiv ID present. Unverified status is a pipeline miss rather than a fabricated citation.

takeaways: Verified does not mean clean extraction: several verified rows have unreadable titles but correct identity via arXiv ID.
Unverified often still means a real paper: 4/5 spot-checked failures had valid arXiv IDs; only #25 is a pure parse failure.
BERT (1810.04805) failed earlier: pdfplumber text joins 'References' to the first citation on one line, so the references-section regex never fires.
